title: Server route mounts and middleware order (server.ts)
summary: Express app order: helmet, cors, express.json and urlencoded (10mb each), GET /api/health (no auth), then 14 router mounts each wrapped with authenticateUser (projects, projectAssets, sceneAssets, shotAssignments, frames, checkout, stageStates, streamline, sceneStageLocks under /api/projects; llm, seed, style-capsules, images, assets). errorHandler is registered last. There is no 404 handler and no rate limiter. The server listens unless NODE_ENV is 'test'.
notes: All 15 route modules in backend/src/routes are mounted; health is the only unauthenticated router (health.ts:5-12).

title: authenticateUser runs once per /api/projects mount traversed (5 to 9 Supabase Auth calls per request)
summary: authenticateUser reads the Bearer token and calls supabase.auth.getUser(token) with the service-role client, which is a network round trip to Supabase Auth per call. Because the same middleware is passed to each /api/projects router mount, a request that matches a later router passes through every earlier mount's middleware. Matching checkout routes runs 6 validations; matching sceneStageLocks routes runs 9. Requests with no Bearer header return 401 before any network call.
notes: Multiplicity follows Express app.use semantics (a middleware runs for every matching layer that calls next). Count per route family is derived from mount order, not measured at runtime.

title: Ownership: families with an explicit projects.user_id or helper check
summary: Explicit ownership checks (project lookup with .eq('user_id', userId) or equivalent) exist in: checkout (all 8 routes), frames (all 27), projectAssets (all 37), sceneStageLocks (4), stageStates (6), streamline (7), projects (all project-scoped routes), assets (7, global assets by user), styleCapsules (filter .or(user_id.eq.X,is_preset.eq.true) for reads, user_id compare for writes), shotAssignments (8; verifyProjectOwnership checks project, then scene existence, then branch.project_id), images GET /jobs/:jobId (project or global asset ownership). Route checks bind the path projectId only; sub-resource IDs in bodies and paths are mostly not bound to the project (see ROUTE-04 to ROUTE-06).

flags.tested: P: only shotLocking and referenceContinuity tests mount auth-guarded routers

Loose pass (any userId or user_id mention in handler body) flags 20 handlers: health 1, llm 11 (utility and template routes, see ROUTE-07), sceneAssets transformation-events 7 (true gap, see ROUTE-04), seed 1. title: image_generation_jobs lifecycle (in-process, single attempt, no sweeper)
summary: Creation inserts a queued row and returns jobId immediately; executeJobInBackground runs unawaited (.catch logs only). Transitions: queued to processing (sets processing_started_at, attempt_count hard-set to 1, last_attempt_at), to generating, to uploading, then completed (storage_path, public_url, cost_credits, completed_at) or failed (error_code, error_message, failure_stage). failure_stage is derived from the DB status at failure: uploading gives uploading, generating gives generating, anything else (including failures before generating) is labelled persisting. There is no job-level retry and no startup reconciliation.

notes: Line numbers for the processing/generating/uploading updates are approximate ranges around the cited blocks; the transition calls themselves are verified. Global asset path (ImageGenerationService.ts:736-935) follows the same pattern and additionally bumps global_assets.version non-atomically (read at :867, write at :873-885).

title: video_generation_jobs lifecycle, auto-retry (3 attempts) and manual retry
summary: confirm-render inserts queued rows (one per shot with a start frame URL) and then fires the global executor. The executor moves a job to processing (processing_started_at), increments attempt_count with a separate write, then generating, uploading (provider_job_id recorded after the provider already uploaded) and completed (video_url, storage_path, actual_cost, completed_at). On failure, if the attempt count is below max_retries (default 3) it goes back to queued with error_message; otherwise it goes to failed. Manual retry only accepts failed rows, sets queued and clears error and provider fields but leaves attempt_count, so a retried job gets one attempt. The retryable flag on provider errors is ignored.

title: Global in-process video executor loop (serial, memory flag, no row claim, no startup hook)
summary: A single VideoJobExecutor instance holds an in-memory isProcessing flag. processQueuedJobs loops: select the oldest queued row across all users (fetchNextQueuedJob), process it, sleep 500 ms, repeat. A second trigger while running is a no-op, but the running loop keeps polling and picks up new rows. There is no row lock or conditional claim (select by status queued, then update by id only). DB errors in the fetch are treated as an empty queue. Any exception escaping processJob (for example a failed status write in the failure branch) ends the loop and leaves the job in its last written status. Nothing calls processQueuedJobs at startup, and pollIntervalMs is declared but unused.

notes: Grep for processQueuedJobs returns one call site (videoGenerationService.ts:417, inside triggerJobProcessing). Grep for setInterval, setImmediate and process.on in backend/src (non-test) returned none.

title: frames.status for start and end frame image jobs (write paths and the unreachable reconciliation)
summary: Frame generation sets frames.status to generating and current_job_id. On image job success, the executor itself updates the frame row to generated with image_url and storage_path. On image job failure, nothing writes the frame, so it stays generating. The only code that reconciles a failed frame to rejected, or accrues image cost into frames.total_cost_credits, is getFrameJobStatus behind GET /frames/:frameId/status. No UI code calls that route, so in the shipped UI the failed frame stays generating and total_cost_credits is never increased.

title: scenes.status becomes video_complete when all scene video jobs complete (never reset)
summary: After each job reaches completed or final failed, checkAndUpdateSceneStatus loads all jobs for the scene; if every job is completed it sets scenes.status to video_complete. Partial or failed sets are logged only. The value is never reset, including when a later confirm-render adds jobs.
notes: Uses all historical rows for the scene, so duplicate jobs from re-confirm also gate completion.

title: user_credits: lazy creation, single deduction at confirm, no refund or top-up
summary: ensureUserCredits inserts a 100.00 row on first balance read, which happens on any Stage 11 load. confirm-render deducts the whole scene total (video cost for every shot including skipped ones, plus frame costs) after inserting queued rows, using a non-atomic read-modify-write on balance. Failed jobs, skipped shots and actual-versus-estimate differences are never refunded or reconciled. addCredits has no caller, so no top-up path exists.

title: Idempotency keys: internal callers append Date.now(), so dedupe never matches
summary: createImageJob looks up an existing row by (project_id, idempotency_key) before inserting, backed by a unique partial index. Every internal caller builds its key as a prefix plus Date.now(), so the key is effectively unique per call and the lookup never returns a row. The global asset path stores the key but never looks it up. Confirm-render, manual video retry and frame regenerate have no dedupe at all. Net effect: double submissions create duplicate jobs and charges.

summary: Backend reads: PORT (default 3001, server.ts:28), NODE_ENV (server.ts:35,95; errorHandler.ts:18,26; health.ts:11; no default), SUPABASE_URL and SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY (required, config/supabase.ts:9-10), SUPABASE_ANON_KEY (read, exported as supabaseConfig, never imported, config/supabase.ts:27), GOOGLE_AI_API_KEY (required by LLMClient, NanoBananaClient and ImageAnalysisService; llm-client.ts:75,134; NanoBananaClient.ts:21; imageAnalysisService.ts:25), GEMINI_MODEL (llm-client.ts:76,106,310; default per site), LANGSMITH_API_KEY (required by LLMClient, llm-client.ts:83,95-99,156), LANGSMITH_TRACING (llm-client.ts:156; also read by @langchain/core), VIDEO_PROVIDER (default 'mock', createVideoProvider.ts:18), GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT (required for Veo, Veo3Provider.ts:41) and GOOGLE_CLOUD_LOCATION (default us-central1, Veo3Provider.ts:42). Frontend reads VITE_SUPABASE_URL and VITE_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY only. GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS is read by no code (ADC implicit).
notes: Test-only: E2E_EMAIL, E2E_PASSWORD, E2E_PROJECT_ID (e2e/*.spec.ts), TEST_AUTH_TOKEN, TEST_PROJECT_ID, TEST_SCENE_ID (backend/src/tests/shotLocking4_5_task_11.test.ts), CI (playwright.config.ts:19-20), GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS and TEST_* in veo3-test.ts. Scripts also read SUPABASE_URL and SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY (backend/scripts/*). Names in env examples with no reader are recorded as H-PROV-09.

title: CORS allowlist: production uses a placeholder origin; dev origins exclude the actual Vite port
summary: cors() allows origin ['https://your-frontend-domain.com'] when NODE_ENV is production, and ['http://localhost:5173','http://localhost:3000'] otherwise, with credentials true. Vite serves on 8080, so direct dev cross-origin calls would be rejected; the proxy avoids this. In production any real frontend origin other than the placeholder is refused by CORS.

flags.functional: P: dev unaffected by proxy; production origin unset

notes: fly.toml sets NODE_ENV=production (fly.toml:7-8), so the placeholder list is active on the deployed API.

title: Request limits and upload handling: JSON 10 MB, multer in-memory with per-route caps
summary: express.json and urlencoded limit bodies to 10 MB. Seven multer configurations use memoryStorage (never disk) with per-route fileSize caps: 5 MB (frames, sceneAssets, styleCapsules), 10 MB (projectAssets, assets, streamline image), and 20 MB (streamline document). Helmet 7.2.0 applies default headers. No rate limiter, no compression, no CSRF token (auth is a Bearer header, not cookies).
notes: multer.memoryStorage() count across routes: 7 (verified). No rateLimit or express-rate-limit import (grep).

title: Error handling: route-level catch and JSON responses; global handler reached only via next(err)
summary: Routes handle errors inline: 214 catch blocks and roughly 327 res.status(500) responses across route files, most returning the error message. The global errorHandler is reached only through next(err), which in this codebase happens for body-parser failures (malformed JSON, oversize body) and synchronous throws; the only other next() call is authenticateUser's success path. Express 4.22.1 does not forward async rejections, so 197 of 198 handlers rely on their own try blocks; the one exception is the sync health route. The process has no unhandledRejection, uncaughtException or SIGTERM handler.

flags.functional: P: async escapes not analyzed outside try blocks

notes: Counts from grep over backend/src/routes (route handlers 198 from registration scan; catch blocks 214; res.status(500) 327). Grep for process.on, SIGTERM, SIGINT in backend/src (non-test) returned none.

title: Error response shape is inconsistent across layers; frontend parsing can stringify objects
summary: authenticateUser and most routes return { error: string }. errorHandler returns { error: { message, code, stack (dev only) } }. checkoutService and frameService read error.error and pass it to new Error, so a body from errorHandler would produce an object-derived message. Only body-parser errors reach errorHandler, so the mismatch is rare in practice.
notes: Frontend message fallback only applies when error.error is falsy; with an object it is truthy.

title: Frontend error surfaces: two toast systems, silent catches, no error boundary, default QueryClient
summary: Two toast systems are mounted (sonner in 30 files and shadcn use-toast in 17 files; both Toaster components are rendered in App.tsx). There are 202 catch blocks in non-test src: 19 are comment-only (silent) and 31 only log to console. There is no ErrorBoundary or componentDidCatch, so an uncaught render error unmounts the tree. QueryClient is created with defaults, so query errors surface only where a component renders them. No 401 or 403 handling exists in the client.
notes: Silent catch counts come from a brace-matching scan of catch bodies; comment-only means no statement inside the catch block. Stage 6 catches render-status failures silently by design (comment says non-critical).

title: Backend catch-block census and silent-failure sites
summary: backend/src (non-test) has 290 catch blocks: 7 are comment-only (routes/frames.ts:573 and :2220; services/frameGenerationService.ts:786; services/promptGenerationService.ts:1493; utils/llmJson.ts:44, :80, :100) and 22 only log. Silent catches in frames.ts and frameGenerationService.ts sit on delete and cleanup paths.
notes: Scan used brace matching over non-test .ts files. Individual sites not each read in full; classification is by catch body only.

title: Storage bucket map: asset-images is the workhorse; videos is referenced but never created; frames delete targets a bucket never written
summary: asset-images is referenced by about 20 backend upload, read, or remove sites (image jobs, uploads, localizer, attempts). style-capsule-images is written by styleCapsules.ts:389-402. videos is written only by Veo3Provider (lines 338 and 354) and no migration or script creates it. frames is used only for remove at routes/frames.ts:1465, while uploads for the same objects go to asset-images (frames.ts:1109-1122); that remove call is awaited without checking its error, and the job row is deleted afterwards.

flags.functional: P: delete path leaves objects behind

notes: Bucket existence in the live Supabase project is UNKNOWN (no repo evidence for videos or frames). grep for the literal 'videos' in backend/migrations and quickies-sql returned no table or bucket creation.

title: Logging is console-only; no logger, metrics, tracing SDK beyond LangChain, or structured sink
summary: Backend diagnostics use console.log and console.error throughout. No winston, pino or morgan dependency is declared or imported. Timestamps are added manually only in errorHandler. There is no request logging middleware. Visibility of background job failures therefore depends on stdout capture on the host.
notes: grep for winston, pino and morgan in backend/src returned no matches (verified).

title: Deployment artifacts: Fly.io config for the API only; no Dockerfile, CI workflow or frontend host config in repo
summary: backend/fly.toml names app wizardirector-api, builds with the Paketo nodejs buildpack, sets NODE_ENV=production, exposes internal_port 3001 over HTTPS with force_https, enables auto_stop_machines and auto_start_machines with min_machines_running 0, and allocates one shared CPU with 1024 MB. It defines no http checks, no PORT, no VIDEO_PROVIDER, and no Google variables. Backend start is node dist/server.js after tsc (tsconfig includes src/** so tests compile into dist). No .github directory, Dockerfile, Procfile or frontend hosting config exists in the repo.
notes: Health route /api/health exists (H-ROUTE-10) but is not referenced by fly.toml. No engines field pins Node. Ls of repo root and git ls-files show no CI or host config.

title: Scripts and config: npm script inventory, lint and migrate caveats
summary: Root scripts: dev (vite), build, build:dev, lint (eslint .), preview, test (vitest run), test:watch, test:e2e (playwright), test:e2e:ui. Backend scripts: dev (tsx watch src/server.ts), build (tsc), start (node dist/server.js), lint (eslint src/**/*.ts), test (jest), test:connectivity (tsx src/tests/connectivity-test.ts), migrate (tsx scripts/run-migrations.ts, not run), setup:bucket. Backend has no eslint config file, so the backend lint script depends on ESLint 8 discovery and was not run (UNKNOWN). The migrate script splits each SQL file on semicolons and calls rpc('exec'), which no migration defines.

flags.functional: U: lint and migrate not executed

notes: Migrate script is documented here, not executed (project rule forbids running it). playwright.config.ts loads a root .env file that does not exist in this checkout, and defines no webServer (dev servers assumed running). Vite config sets vitest include to src/**/*.{test,spec}.{ts,tsx} with jsdom and src/test/setup.ts.

title: Test harness: backend jest loads backend/.env, frontend vitest is jsdom, e2e has 2 specs; auth coverage is thin
summary: Backend jest (ts-jest ESM, testMatch limited to src/tests and src/**/__tests__) loads backend/.env via dotenv in jest.setup.ts and sets NODE_ENV=test if unset, so tests that import real services may reach real providers. Backend has 41 test files, frontend 26, e2e 2 specs. Auth enforcement is tested only in shotLocking4_5_task_11.test.ts (401 cases) and no test covers the transformation-events, llm template, or seed routes. llm-integration.test.ts reaches real Gemini and LangSmith without an environment gate (wave1 E).
notes: Test file counts from find over backend/src (41) and src (26). The real-provider test was not opened in this pass (wave1 E claim, unverified here).

title: Diagnostic endpoint exposes style capsule internals to owner or preset readers
summary: GET /api/images/debug-style-capsule/:capsuleId returns descriptor strings, design pillars and reference image URLs for a capsule that is the caller's or a preset. It is mounted under the normal authenticated image router and is not gated by environment.
notes: Ownership check is present (is_preset or user_id equals caller), so this is not a cross-tenant read; it is a debug surface reachable in production builds.

title: Module-scope side effects and env loading order
summary: config/supabase.ts calls dotenv.config() only when SUPABASE_URL is unset at its import time, and dotenv reads .env relative to process.cwd(). server.ts calls dotenv.config() at line 25, but its ES module imports (routes and services, including the module-scope constructions in H-FACT-04) are evaluated before that line runs. Running the server from the repo root therefore does not load backend/.env, while running from backend/ does, provided SUPABASE_URL is still unset.
notes: Derived from ES module evaluation order and dotenv defaults; not executed.

title: Frontend session and token attachment pattern
summary: Each service method calls supabase.auth.getSession() and attaches Authorization Bearer <access_token>; checkoutService throws 'User not authenticated' when no session exists. Requests are not retried on 401, and the frontend never refreshes tokens explicitly (supabase-js autoRefreshToken handles it in the background).
notes: Count of getSession sites is 157 (grep). Some services also pass a token obtained once and reuse it through a polling loop (projectAssetService.pollImageJob accepts accessToken, :385-395); a token older than one hour could expire during a long poll (inference, not tested).

title: SUPABASE_ANON_KEY is read and exported but never consumed
summary: config/supabase.ts reads SUPABASE_ANON_KEY into supabaseConfig.anonKey, with a comment that it is exported for client-side usage. Nothing imports supabaseConfig, and the browser uses VITE_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY instead.
notes: Grep for supabaseConfig across backend/src and scripts returned the definition only.

title: All background work lives in the API process; no recovery exists for non-terminal rows
summary: Image jobs, global asset jobs and the video executor run as unawaited promises inside the Express process. No queue, worker, cron, pg_cron, webhook, startup reconciliation or stale-job sweeper exists in repo code or SQL. A restart, crash or machine stop strands image rows in processing, generating or uploading, video rows in processing, generating or uploading, and frames stuck in generating. Retry refuses non-failed video rows, so those are permanent. fly.toml sets auto_stop_machines true and min_machines_running 0.

flags.functional: P: works until the process exits

evidence: backend/migrations (grep: no cron, pg_net, http_request, webhook)
notes: Fly auto-stop semantics are platform behavior not verified in the repo. Inference: in-flight promises do not hold HTTP connections, so the platform may stop the machine mid-job. Stage 12 polls forever on a stranded job (STATE-10).

title: Single-process assumption for the video loop; no row claim
summary: The video executor guards with an in-memory flag and claims work by select-then-update-by-id. If two API instances run, both can select the same queued row and both process it, generating duplicate provider calls and duplicate cost. Deployment instance count is not set in the repo (fly.toml has no scale or count), so the actual count is UNKNOWN.

flags.reachable: P: needs more than one instance
flags.persisted: Y: duplicate rows and provider spend

notes: Image jobs have no claim step either but each job is created and run by the request that created it, so duplication requires a duplicate request.

title: No concurrency limit on image or video provider calls beyond the serial video loop
summary: Each image job request spawns an unawaited executeJobInBackground with no semaphore, queue, or per-user limit, so parallel Gemini image calls scale with request volume (the only limit is the 4-attempt retry inside the client). Video calls are serial per process, and their submit and poll share the same loop, so one slow Veo job blocks all queued videos for every user.
notes: Grep for p-limit, semaphore, concurren, mutex, pLimit, maxConcurrent, rateLimit in backend/src (non-test) returned no matches.

title: Retry and manual retry cannot dedupe or limit spend (charged jobs re-run without a cap)
summary: Auto-retry re-runs the full paid provider call up to three times for every error class, including PERMANENT safety-filter or bad-model errors that the provider classified as non-retryable. Manual retry of a failed Veo job runs one more paid call with no credit check, no charge recording, and no attempt reset. Duplicate confirm-render also re-queues and re-charges the whole scene with no existing-job check.
notes: Charge and provider spend per failed attempt are inferred from the provider call structure (Veo bills per generation under the design of the call); billing terms are external and not verified.

title: Client timeouts end before server work does, and the UI loops never end on stranded states
summary: Client budgets for image jobs (60 to 120 seconds) end before the server has any deadline, so the UI can show a timeout while the job continues and later writes the asset. Conversely, Stage 10 and Stage 12 loops poll with no ceiling and continue forever on stranded frames or jobs. Server-side, Veo has a 5-minute poll cap, and the video retry loop can then resubmit a paid job up to three times.
notes: Veo timeout returns TEMPORARY (Veo3Provider.ts:296-298), which the executor retries as a fresh paid submission.
